title: DPM-NLL: exact discrete log-det of the deployed DPM-Solver trajectory via residual Hutchinson
one_liner: Pair DDIM-NLL's instantaneous change-of-variables with DPM-Solver's exponential integrator so the reported NLL is the exact determinant of the deployed discrete sampler — not a continuous-limit approximation — at a fraction of the trace-estimator VJPs.
description: DPM-Solver is a fast sampler with no likelihood machinery: it integrates the probability-flow ODE with an exact linear part and reaches target sample quality in ~10–20 steps. DDIM-NLL supplies the missing density machinery — instantaneous change-of-variables plus a Hutchinson trace per step — but only as a first-order, Euler-flavored estimate that spends one backward-mode VJP per step and approaches the true density only in the continuous limit. The composition: run DPM-Solver (multi-step form) as the backbone, contribute the linear part of every step to the log-determinant in closed form, and apply the residual Hutchinson estimator only to the nonlinear score part. The interface is the work: a naive sum of Δt·div along a DPM-Solver trajectory is not the determinant of the solver's discrete map, because higher-order steps contain cross-Jacobian trace terms tr(J_i J_j) that separate traces miss — so the likelihood would lag the sampler's own order of accuracy. Decomposing solver steps into composing first-order substeps (as the multi-step variants do) turns the log-det into a sum of per-step affine+score determinants, with any remaining cross-term estimated by one coupled double-VJP. The payoff: matched accuracy at 5–10× fewer VJPs, and — unlike both the base Euler estimate and an FFJORD-style fine ODE — an NLL for the exact sampler the model actually deploys.

sections.technique: Use deterministic DPM-Solver-2M/DPM-Solver++ (η=0) with K≈10–20 steps. Each step, given cached score evaluations, is affine-plus-score: x_{i+1} = a_i x_i + Σ_j b_{ij} ε_θ(x_cached). Accumulate log|det| = Σ_i [ d·log|a_i| + log|det(I + a_i^{-1} Σ_j b_{ij} J_{ij})| ], with J_{ij} the input Jacobian of ε_θ at the cached point; first-order truncation in the b coefficients, plus optional second-order cross-terms via coupled Hutchinson (a JVP through the inner evaluation then a VJP through the outer — one double backward pass per cross-term). Use Rademacher vectors, a few Hutchinson samples per step, shared/antithetic seeds across steps to tame accumulated variance, and report mean±std over seeds. Validate on CIFAR-10 / ImageNet-64 against a fine-grid FFJORD-style ODE NLL and the long-run SDE ELBO; plot NLL gap vs step count and count VJPs at matched NLL error.
open_questions: Does DPM-Solver's step-count advantage transfer to the trace-estimator budget at matched likelihood accuracy, or is likelihood error dominated by log-det truncation rather than sample error?
Is the coupled-Hutchinson estimate of tr(J_i J_j) stable, and does the 2M substep decomposition make these cross-terms unnecessary in practice?
Are the per-step Jacobians a_i I + Σ b_ij J_ij well-conditioned at the large h values DPM-Solver uses, so the accumulated log-det does not drift?
Which parameterization (ε- vs v-prediction) yields the smallest b coefficients and therefore the tightest first-order truncation?
Is the exact discrete log-det of the deployed sampler the quantity practitioners want, or does it deliberately conflate sampler bias with model quality?
sections.rationale: Combiner stance: I fuse two explicitly named methods — DDIM-NLL's instantaneous change-of-variables (density machinery, but first-order and one VJP per step) and DPM-Solver's exponential integrator (fast, accurate, but has no likelihood concept). Each supplies what the other lacks, and the composition (solver backbone + closed-form linear-part determinant + residual Hutchinson on the nonlinear part) is the contribution. The efficiency argument is the central one: DPM-Solver's ~10–20 step accuracy means the dominant VJP budget drops by roughly an order of magnitude. The 'what breaks when naively stacked' point is the interface work: a naive continuous-limit log-det sum is not the discrete map's determinant for higher-order solvers because of cross-Jacobian trace terms, and the fix (substep decomposition / coupled Hutchinson) is the actual novel engineering. Unverified claims to flag: the ~10–20-step accuracy equivalence of DPM-Solver is asserted from its paper, not re-derived here; that DPM-Solver-2M is exactly a composition of affine+score substeps whose log-det is a sum should be checked against Lu et al. 2022's update equations; and that per-step VJPs dominate the cost of the base DDIM-NLL is assumed from the base idea's own framing.
